meaning: AWS's managed Kubernetes: AWS runs the control plane and you run pods on nodes in your account.
A countable thing beyond CPU and memory that a node advertises and a pod claims in whole units, such as nvidia.com/gpu.
The state of a pod that no node can hold yet; on a cluster that scales from zero it is the request for a machine.
The open-source node autoscaler AWS builds: it launches EC2 instances for pending pods and removes instances no longer needed.
The Karpenter object that says which instances may be launched, how many, and when nodes may be removed.
The Karpenter object holding the AWS settings for nodes: image, role, subnets, security groups, disks, reservations.
Karpenter's record of one instance on its way to being a node: Launched, Registered, Initialized.
The purchase option a NodePool allows: spot, on-demand or reserved (capacity reservations).
A taint marks a node so that only pods declaring a matching toleration may be scheduled on it.
The EC2 API that fills one capacity request from a list of instance types.
The Spot allocation strategy that takes the lowest-priced pools among those with the most spare capacity.
Karpenter removing or replacing nodes to cut cost.
A node no longer matching its NodePool or image, which makes Karpenter replace it.
The Amazon SQS queue through which Karpenter receives EC2 events such as the Spot interruption warning.
An EC2 signal that a Spot instance is at elevated risk of interruption; it can arrive before the two-minute warning.
The signal that asks a process to stop; a pod receives it when it is evicted and has its grace period to finish.
A Kubernetes add-on that holds Jobs until a quota has room and then lets them create their pods.
The Kueue object that describes one kind of node through node labels and tolerations.
The Kueue object that holds a quota per flavor for the whole cluster.
The Kueue object a team submits to in its namespace; it points at one ClusterQueue.
The unit Kueue admits; it creates one for each Job.
A group of ClusterQueues that lend each other unused quota.
A Kubernetes scheduler for GPU work with hierarchical queues, gang scheduling and fractional GPUs.
Scheduling all of a job's pods together or none of them.
A Kubernetes object that runs a group of Jobs as one unit and restarts them together.
The Kubeflow Trainer object a user submits; it points at an administrator's runtime template.
A DaemonSet that advertises a node's devices to Kubernetes; the NVIDIA one advertises GPUs as nvidia.com/gpu.
A Kubernetes object that runs one pod on every matching node.
NVIDIA's package that installs the driver, toolkit, device plugin, node labelling and monitoring together.
An NVIDIA feature that runs several processes on one GPU at the same moment.
A hardware feature that splits one GPU into isolated instances, each with its own memory and compute.
Several pods taking turns on one GPU, with no memory or compute isolation.
The Kubernetes API in which a driver publishes devices with attributes and a pod claims one by description.
The EKS option in which AWS runs the node layer: managed Karpenter, image, GPU driver and plugin, Spot handling, repair.
The disk image an EC2 instance boots from.
The AWS service whose sessions give shell access to an instance without SSH.
The NVIDIA driver's numbered report of a GPU fault.
NVIDIA's direct GPU-to-GPU connection.
The plug-in form in which Kubernetes mounts storage into pods as volumes.

term: Mountpoint for Amazon S3 CSI driver
meaning: The driver that presents an S3 bucket as a volume in a pod.
A managed parallel file system for many nodes reading and writing large files at once.
The EC2 network device that lets training processes on different nodes exchange data without the operating system's network stack.
A hold on EC2 instances of one type.
GPU instances booked for a fixed window.
The EC2 GPU instance families whose names start with g, such as g5, g6, g6e and g7e.
The P6e machines that join many GPUs with NVLink.
A number from 1 to 10 for how likely a Spot request is to succeed in a Region or zone.
The unit in which EC2 counts processor capacity and Spot quotas.
NVIDIA's workflow orchestrator for physical AI pipelines across training, simulation and edge computers.
On-premises or edge machines joined to an EKS cluster as nodes while AWS runs the control plane.
